name: Vibe coding workshop with Lovable — NEOMA
description: A hands-on workshop at NEOMA Business School to introduce students to vibe coding and the rise of no-code: each team picked a small local business with no website and built a website proposal for it in one hour with Lovable.
context: Most business students have never built software. The goal of the workshop was to show them that this has changed: with AI-assisted "vibe coding" tools, describing what you want in plain language is enough to get a working website, which opens product building to non-developers.
The workshop was held at NEOMA Business School with the Build Challenge NEOMA student community.

work.title: The challenge
work.text: Choose a real business or small shop that has no website, and build it a website proposal in one hour.
points: Pick the business and understand what its customers need to find online.
Prompt Lovable to generate the site, then iterate on sections, content and design.
Present the result to the room.

work.title: What students saw in practice
work.text: Beyond the visual result, the demos showed what the tool produces under the hood: a real code base with components, assets and SEO tags (title, description, Open Graph, structured data), and features such as a booking system that need a back end to go live.

work.title: Key takeaway
work.text: No-code and AI tools turn an idea into a usable prototype in an hour. The value moves to choosing the right problem, writing clear instructions and judging the result.

items.alt: Two students presenting their Lovable project, a website for a local butcher's shop, on a projected screen showing the generated code during the vibe coding workshop at NEOMA
